answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission: each agent identity must keep inter-request timing noise ("jitter delta") within a tight band; a controller measures variance against a rolling baseline and flags flat, machine-regular cadence. A single slow drifting clock (a "vine" of timed pings) seeds the baseline, so bursts must stay phase-locked across the "ocean" of nodes rather than spiking freely. Enforcement: flagged identities are throttled to one request per epoch. The attacker pays a per-identity latency floor plus ongoing clock-sync maintenance.
